newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Bullion's slide to its weakest level in over four years winded South African gold shares, tearing three percent off the index at the close and wounding marginal mines specialist Randgold.

But industrial stocks turned a blind eye to the gold board's woes surging to new peaks as share prices were inflated by Monday's quarter close-out for many unit trusts and heavy early morning futures arbitrage dealings.
Dealers and analysts said that in addition to bullion's fall to $334, gold shares were further pressured by bleak prospects for the South African industry's second quarter results.
"The quarterly results are going to be the worst that the industry has ever seen," said Nick Goodwin, an analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.

"If you agglomerate all the mines' results it will be a net loss. We have never had that before," he said adding, he expected a net loss of 100 million rand compared with a profit of 280 million rand in the first quarter of the year.
Results for the quarter ended June 30, begin pouring in next week with Gold Fields kicking off on Thursday.
The all gold index fell 29.8 points to 965.0, its lowest level since March 1993, dragged down by a 12 percent slide in Randgold to a fresh 1997 low of 20.00 rand -- a drop of 275 cents.
Analysts and dealers said that the main factor behind the poor quarterly showing would be the lower gold price, which would hit even harder when translated into rand terms.
"In previous quarters one had the depreciation of the rand against the dollar to boost the (rand) gold price, but in the last quarter the rand has held fairly steady," a dealer said.
Despite the sag in the index, dealers said that there had been no major sell-off in shares.
"There is not a huge selling push. It's more of a protracted drift down."
Gold near-month futures were also down and were in late trading holding at 650/75 from 680 settlement on Friday.
Industrial shares were the object of "window-dressing", where prices are over-inflated, as funds which did not close their second quarters on Friday did so on Monday.
This activity boosted a number of heavyweight stocks, including Richemont, which added 175 cents to 66.75 rand and Amic which put on 200 cents to 199 rand.
The industrial index finished at a fresh closing high of 8,790.5, a gain of 42.9 points and lifting the all-share index nine points to 7,420.0.
Futures arbitrage trading also helped to boost industrial stocks as players exploited the hefty premium of futures over the spot market to buy shares.
As futures were sold off in favour of stocks the near-month industrial contract fell to last hold at 8,585/600 from 8,631 and the all-share September contract to 6,790/820 from 6,865.

A tiny 100-share trade in clothing firm Rex Trueform caused a stir on the Johannesburg bourse when Syfrets Securities bought the stock at a massive premium of 184 rand compared with the firm's closing share price on Friday of 5.30 rand.

The trade propelled the market's clothing and footwear index over 40 percent, but the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said later that affected indices had been readjusted to exclude the trade although the deal had not been reversed.
Toco leapt 36 percent to 49 cents on perceptions the firm may be on a recovery after it reported a narrower year loss.

Views were mixed on market direction for Tuesday with some dealers worried about possible further weakness in the rand which touched five-month lows ahead of the easing of foreign exchange controls on private individuals on Tuesday.
But others were upbeat on the positive outlook for an interest rate cut.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
